name: Nationality by Descent (Recognition, up to 3rd Degree)

qualifying_event.description: Ecuadorian nationality by descent extends up to the third degree of direct-line consanguinity -- i.e. children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren of an Ecuadorian national -- born abroad. Nationality is not automatic in practice: it must be registered with an Ecuadorian consulate abroad, or with the General Directorate of Civil Registry (DGRCIC) in Ecuador if not done consularly. There is no stated registration deadline.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Apostilled birth certificate(s) (with Spanish translation if needed) establishing the direct-line chain of descent; proof of the Ecuadorian ancestor's identity/nationality; for grandparent/great-grandparent claims, additional ancestral documentation.

requirements.blocker_text: Must be a direct-line descendant (child, grandchild, or great-grandchild) of an Ecuadorian national, up to the third degree of consanguinity.
Must be registered before an Ecuadorian consulate abroad, or before the DGRCIC in Ecuador if not done consularly.
requirements.fix_path: Apply to register the birth/descent with an Ecuadorian consulate or the DGRCIC.

evidence_required.document: Apostilled birth certificate(s) establishing the descent chain
Proof of the Ecuadorian ancestor's identity/nationality
Spanish translation of foreign-language documents (where required)

sources.title: gob.ec (DGRCIC -- General Directorate of Civil Registry, Identification and Cedulation official portal) -- Registration of birth abroad / recognition of nationality: extends to the third degree of direct-line consanguinity, no stated registration deadline

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Ecuador). Notably broader than most descent-citizenship routes in this dataset: Ecuador extends recognition to the THIRD degree of direct lineage (great-grandchildren), not just first-generation children of a citizen parent -- a genuinely distinctive feature worth flagging, consistent with Ecuador's reputation as an accessible ancestry-citizenship option. The tier-1 source does not address whether this three-degree extension itself has any further sub-conditions (e.g. whether the intermediate generations must also have registered) -- not independently resolved in this pass.
